news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Some men are demanding “prince treatment” in the dating world, according to a dating trend making headlines, with men expecting women to pay for meals and spoil them.

Cosmopolitan magazine relationships writer Syeda Khaula Saad dubbed men with these expectations “bratty men” in a piece published in early November.

VICE, meanwhile, reported that the debate over “who’s supposed to spoil whom” has gotten out of hand.

According to the publications, “bratty men” are turning the concept of “princess treatment” on its head.

Men who want “prince treatment” expect pampering, extra attention and gifts. The trend is a reversal of “princess treatment,” the notion that women should be spoiled with flowers, love notes and other romantic gestures.

“I’ve seen countless women sharing their experiences with what I’m now calling ‘bratty men.’ They’re demanding to have their meals paid for, that women drive them around and whatever this is,” Saad wrote Nov. 9.

“They’re announcing that they’re ‘the prize’ and that a woman, or a date, should be spoiling them.”

Toronto publication Now Toronto asked residents to weigh in on the “prince treatment” trend, highlighting a video by Toronto-based TikTok creator Shaurya Manocha arguing that men deserve to be spoiled.

“I would want my daughter to have somebody treat her like the princess that she is … I take care of her, I cherish her — same thing with my wife,” a father and husband told Now Toronto.

Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy was asked about the “bratty men” trend during an interview with Fox Business host Stuart Varney on Wednesday.

Portnoy said he wasn’t sure how much of the trend he believed, asking, “What type of woman would ever want this, or go out with this?”

“This seems a made-up thing,” he added. “I haven’t seen anywhere in my travels that women are willingly or wanting to pick up the check and pick up after and be treated like garbage. So, I hope this trend isn’t real.”

Susan Trombetti, matchmaker and CEO of Exclusive Matchmaking, told Fox News Digital in a statement, “The bratty men and bratty women are out there. It’s a competition of the brats and a response to the women who expect the guy’s first-class upgrade.

“All the social media influencers and podcasters are trying to up the ante to get subscribers and promote this idea that men should be the ones on the pedestal. Your normal, nice guy that can’t get a date or find someone is vulnerable to this sort of nonsense. They figure, ‘Why not give it a try?’

“Women are demanding Ubers and gifts on dates, so why can’t they sit back and demand, too? The problem is that neither the men nor the women who do this are high-value partners.”

She called the idea “ridiculous” and said healthy relationships require give-and-take. Trombetti also said the “bratty men” trend likely wasn’t too prevalent.

“I think it’s more of a social media narrative where influencers try to get the most views and go viral,” she said.

Relationship expert April Davis, founder of Luma Luxury Matchmaking, told Fox News Digital, “A man wanting to be taken out to dinner once in a while isn’t the problem. Why wouldn’t he want that? The question is whether he does thoughtful things for you too or if you’re the one always taking care of him.

“If you want a man who plans dates and picks up the check, you can look for that. If he wants someone who takes turns, that’s fine, too. You may just not be right for each other. There’s no need to turn it into a fight about what all men or all women should do.”

A debate over “princess treatment” spread across social media in July 2025 after a video went viral of a woman explaining what her husband does when the two of them go to a restaurant together.

“If I am at a restaurant with my husband, I do not talk to the hostess, I do not open any doors and I do not order my own food,” the woman said in the video, according to the New York Times.

Some women reacting to the video called it “regressive,” according to the Times. A 26-year-old grad student told the outlet at the time that “princess treatment” can look “however you want it to look.”
news.content: پوشش های بیشتری را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید.بر اساس یک روند قرار ملاقات، برخی از مردان در دنیای دوستیابی خواهان «رفتار با شاهزاده» هستند، و مردان از زنان انتظار دارند که برای وعده های غذایی پول پرداخت کنند و آنها را خراب کنند. سیده خاولا سعد، نویسنده روابط مجلات جهان وطنی، در مقاله ای که در اوایل نوامبر منتشر شد، به مردانی با این انتظارات لقب «مردان بداخلاق» داد. در همین حال، VICE گزارش داد که بحث بر سر "چه کسی قرار است چه کسی را خراب کند" از کنترل خارج شده است. به گفته نشریات، "مردان بداخلاق" مفهوم "درمان با شاهزاده خانم" را بر سر خود می چرخانند. مردانی که خواهان "درمان با شاهزاده" هستند انتظار نوازش، توجه بیشتر و هدایایی دارند. این روند معکوس کردن "رفتار با شاهزاده خانم" است، این تصور که زنان باید با گل، یادداشت های عاشقانه و سایر حرکات عاشقانه لوس شوند. سعد در 9 نوامبر نوشت: «من زنان بی‌شماری را دیده‌ام که تجربیات خود را با آنچه من اکنون «مردان براتی» می‌نامم به اشتراک می‌گذارند. آن‌ها می‌خواهند هزینه وعده‌های غذایی‌شان را پرداخت کنند، زنان آن‌ها را بچرخانند و هر چه که باشد. نشریه تورنتو Now Toronto از ساکنان درخواست کرد تا در مورد روند «درمان با شاهزاده» بسنجید، و ویدیویی توسط Shaurya Manocha خالق TikTok مستقر در تورنتو را برجسته کرد که در آن استدلال می‌کرد که مردان مستحق لوس شدن هستند. «من می‌خواهم دخترم با او مانند شاهزاده خانمی رفتار کند که او است... من از او مراقبت می‌کنم، همان چیزی را که همسرم به همسرم می‌گویم.»

DEAR ABBY: My 70-year-old brother, “Ardal,” called me recently, and I’m still reeling from what he said. He was scammed out of $30,000. Ardal has never been tech-savvy, and he lives a simple life. Even so, the extent of his gullibility is astounding. These thieves knew exactly what to say to allay his suspicions. He literally handed over a bag of $30,000 in cash to a stranger in order to “protect” the rest of his financial assets and “prevent the FBI from arresting him.” Only when the thieves requested an additional $20,000 did my brother finally get wise and go to the police.

The whole thing started when Ardal opened an email he should have deleted. Please advise your readers that these scams are real, and the thieves are on the lookout for naive and trusting people like my brother to prey on. My best piece of advice: If you click on a link and believe you’ve downloaded malware, unplug your computer and take it to a reputable shop. — SAD SISTER

DEAR SISTER: Thank you for your cautionary tale. Readers, if you use a computer for any reason — even if it’s for nothing more than email — it’s imperative that you get training on internet safety. Check with your community centers, senior centers, employers and schools to learn how to prevent this kind of disaster from affecting you.

DEAR ABBY: I have a friend of 40 years. We raised our kids together, planned weddings, welcomed each other’s grandchildren and went on vacations together for years. Her youngest granddaughter was born two years ago, and they live several states away, so we didn’t meet the child until they all gathered for a camping trip near us this past summer. We went to visit them there for the day.

When we arrived and met the little girl, I realized that she had some challenges. She did not walk or talk. I suspect that she has cerebral palsy. My friend never said anything about this to me, either before the visit or after.

I was perplexed by the situation and still don’t know if I should say or ask anything. I am hurt that she never said a thing about the complications they have all been dealing with. Should I say anything or remain silent if or until she mentions it? — DIDN’T KNOW IN NEW YORK

DEAR DIDN’T KNOW: Stop feeling hurt. Your friend may not have discussed the child’s developmental issues with you because the subject is painful for them. Although your intentions are good, I hope you will not bring it up.

DEAR ABBY: My daughter forgot my 75th birthday, and I feel so hurt. I don’t know what to say to her. She’s the mother of two teenage boys and is quite busy. I didn’t expect any gifts and certainly not a party, but I did expect some acknowledgement. What do I say if and when she finally remembers? — FORGOTTEN IN NEW MEXICO

DEAR FORGOTTEN: What you should say is, “Thank you. How sweet of you.” Period. When she finally remembers, she will already feel terrible without any admonishment from you.

Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at http://www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.

بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. ABBY عزیز: برادر 70 ساله من، "اردال" اخیراً با من تماس گرفت و من هنوز از صحبت های او نگران هستم. از او 30 هزار دلار کلاهبرداری کردند. اردال هرگز به فن آوری علاقه نداشته است و زندگی ساده ای دارد. با این حال، میزان زودباوری او حیرت انگیز است. این دزدها دقیقا می دانستند که برای رفع سوء ظن او باید چه بگویند. او به معنای واقعی کلمه یک کیسه 30000 دلاری را به یک غریبه تحویل داد تا از بقیه دارایی های مالی خود محافظت کند و از دستگیری FBI جلوگیری کند. فقط زمانی که دزدها 20000 دلار دیگر درخواست کردند، برادرم بالاخره عاقل شد و به پلیس رفت. همه چیز از زمانی شروع شد که اردال ایمیلی را که باید پاک می کرد باز کرد. لطفا به خوانندگان خود اطلاع دهید که این کلاهبرداری ها واقعی است و سارقان به دنبال افراد ساده لوح و قابل اعتمادی مانند برادر من هستند تا طعمه آنها شوند. بهترین توصیه من: اگر روی پیوندی کلیک می کنید و فکر می کنید بدافزار دانلود کرده اید، رایانه خود را از برق بکشید و آن را به یک فروشگاه معتبر ببرید. - خواهر غمگین
خواهر عزیز: از شما برای داستان هشدار دهنده شما متشکرم. خوانندگان، اگر به هر دلیلی از رایانه استفاده می کنید - حتی اگر برای چیزی جز ایمیل نباشد - ضروری است که در مورد ایمنی اینترنت آموزش ببینید. با مراکز اجتماعی، مراکز ارشد، کارفرمایان و مدارس خود تماس بگیرید تا یاد بگیرید که چگونه از تأثیر این نوع فاجعه جلوگیری کنید. ABBY عزیز: من یک دوست 40 ساله دارم. بچه هایمان را با هم بزرگ کردیم، عروسی برنامه ریزی کردیم، از نوه های همدیگر پذیرایی کردیم و با هم به تعطیلات رفتیم.

news.originalContent:
Rescue crews continue looking for missing workers in destroyed three-story facility near Jakarta.

A fire at a sweets factory in Indonesia has killed at least three people and 36 others are missing.

At least 15 people were rescued from the Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province, which borders the capital Jakarta, including four taken to hospital, said the National Search and Rescue Agency in a statement on Sunday.

“The fire is still burning in several locations and firefighting teams are continuing extinguishing and cooling operations,” rescue official Rizky Dwianto told The Associated Press news agency.

Firefighters from Serang district and Banten province were battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the fire began, Dwianto said.

Rescue workers along with fire department personnel and the Indonesian Red Cross searched different sections of the factory, focusing on areas where victims might be trapped, he added.

Around 60 people were in the factory when the fire started. Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters.

The factory produces milk-based snacks and sweets, known as Milkita.

Photos and videos circulating online captured black flames and thick smoke coming from the three-storey building. Footage from inside appeared to show the fire caused extensive damage, with equipment blackened and destroyed.

Local broadcasters and social media accounts shared footage of families gathering outside the factory.

The disaster agency said the cause of the fire was under investigation.

Indonesia has suffered a number of deadly fires in recent years. A fire in an office building in Jakarta killed at least 22 people last December. An explosion at an Indonesian nickel-processing plant killed at least 13 people in 2023.
news.content: گروه های امداد و نجات به جستجوی کارگران مفقود شده در تاسیسات سه طبقه ویران شده در نزدیکی جاکارتا ادامه می دهند. آتش سوزی در یک کارخانه شیرینی در اندونزی دست کم سه کشته و 36 نفر دیگر ناپدید شده اند. حداقل 15 نفر از کارخانه فونوسا آگونگ مولیا در استان بانتن، که هم مرز با جاکارتا پایتخت است، نجات یافتند، از جمله 4 نفر از آنها به بیمارستان منتقل شدند. ریزکی دویانتو، مسئول امداد و نجات، به خبرگزاری آسوشیتدپرس گفت: «آتش سوزی هنوز در چندین نقطه در حال شعله‌ور است و تیم‌های اطفای حریق به عملیات اطفای و خنک‌سازی ادامه می‌دهند.» به گفته Dwian، بیش از 12 ساعت پس از شروع آتش‌سوزی، آتش‌نشانان منطقه سرانگ و استان بانتن در حال مبارزه با شعله‌های آتش در چندین بخش از تأسیسات بودند. او افزود که نیروهای امدادی به همراه پرسنل آتش نشانی و صلیب سرخ اندونزی بخش های مختلف کارخانه را با تمرکز بر مناطقی که ممکن است قربانیان گرفتار شده باشند، جستجو کردند. حدود 60 نفر هنگام شروع آتش سوزی در کارخانه بودند. آندرا سونی، فرماندار استان بانتن به خبرنگاران گفت. این کارخانه تنقلات و شیرینی های مبتنی بر شیر، معروف به میلکیتا، تولید می کند. عکس‌ها و فیلم‌هایی که در فضای مجازی پخش می‌شوند، شعله‌های سیاه و دود غلیظی را که از ساختمان سه طبقه بیرون می‌آمد، ضبط کرده‌اند. به نظر می رسد که فیلم از داخل نشان می دهد که آتش سوزی خسارات زیادی را به همراه داشته است و تجهیزات سیاه شده و تخریب شده است. پخش کننده های محلی و حساب های رسانه های اجتماعی فیلم هایی از جمع شدن خانواده ها در خارج از کارخانه را به اشتراک گذاشته اند. فاجعه ag

news.originalTitle: Wembanyama scores 50 points, bags 19 rebounds in Spurs’ 14th win of season
news.title: ویمبانیاما در چهاردهمین برد فصل اسپرز 50 امتیاز و 19 ریباند به دست آورد.
news.originalSummary:

news.originalContent:
Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.

Victor Wembanyama has scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds to power San Antonio to a 114-91 victory over New Orleans as the Spurs matched the National Basketball Association’s best record at 14-3.

The 22-year-old, 7-foot-4-inch (2.24m) Frenchman made 20 of 29 shots from the floor, 5 of 11 from three-point range, and added five blocked shots, four steals and an assist in 32 minutes on the court on Saturday.

San Antonio won for the 14th time in 15 games, and Wembanyama became only the third NBA player since the 1973-74 season with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds, four steals and five blocks in a game.

“It is very special, but unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding,” Wembanyama said.

Wembanyama was just shy of his career-high score of 52 points, set in a victory over Dallas on November 4.

“Wemby” scored 17 points in the first quarter as the Spurs jumped to a 32-29 lead over the visiting Pelicans and had 32 points and 13 rebounds at half-time with San Antonio ahead 61-45.

“I thought he started the game off aggressive, and I thought he was trying to play with a lot of force offensively, specifically, just in terms of taking up real estate, trying to get to the rim,” Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.

“I thought he did a really good job of playing with force.”

Johnson did not relish taking Wemby to the bench but wanted to avoid any chance of an injury in a game well in hand.

“Was it tough to pull him out after he got 50? No, I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did,” Johnson said. “That would have been hard to take him out that close to 50.”

The Spurs levelled with the Los Angeles Lakers and Philadelphia 76ers for the best record in the league, the Sixers having matched the mark earlier in a 132-129 victory over Milwaukee.

Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a fifth consecutive victory despite Tyler Herro’s career-high 50 points for the Bucks.

Embiid delivered 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the host Sixers as they dropped the league-worst Bucks to 1-16, stretching Milwaukee’s losing skid to 13 games.

Herro added 11 rebounds and seven assists, but he missed a chance to send the game into overtime.

He sank a three-point shot at the finish, but officials ruled after consulting video replay that the shot left his hand after the final buzzer.

Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player LeBron James scored 21 points, grabbed six rebounds, recorded three steals and provided six assists for the 76ers.

“For us to be a super complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious,” James said. “It’s key for our other guys as well to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident.”

Anfernee Simons added 18 points off the Philadelphia bench while Tyrese Maxey added 17 and VJ Edgecombe scored 16 as the 76ers withstood a late Bucks rally.

“Soon we’re going to have to put together a 48-minute game,” Maxey said.

At Madison Square Garden, Mikal Bridges sank a three-pointer at the final buzzer to give the reigning champions New York Knicks a 97-96 victory over Portland.

The Trail Blazers rallied from a 26-point deficit to seize a 96-94 lead on two free throws by Deni Avdija with 3.2 seconds remaining.

The Knicks tried to inbound the ball to star Jalen Brunson for the last shot but went to Bridges when Brunson was covered.

“They played harder than us in that second half,” Bridges said. “That’s on us, but we just finished the game. It goes 48 minutes, and we just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning.”

The Knicks, without injured starters OG Anunoby and Karl-Anthony Towns, improved to 10-6 with their fourth consecutive victory while Portland fell to 10-6.

Brunson led New York with 30 points, 19 of them in the first quarter, while Landry Shamet added 20 and Bridges had 12 points.

In other games, Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points to lead Minnesota’s 104-95 home win over Memphis, while Kyrie Irving had 25 points and Cooper Flagg added 22 in a 110-100 Dallas home win over the Los Angeles Clippers.

ویمبانیاما با حداقل 50 امتیاز، 15 ریباند، چهار توپ ربایی و پنج بلاک در یک بازی تنها سومین بازیکن NBA از فصل 1973-1974 شد. ویکتور ویمبانیاما با کسب 50 امتیاز و 19 ریباند توانست سن آنتونیو را به پیروزی 114 بر 91 برساند و بهترین رکورد اتحادیه بسکت ملی اسپور در مسابقات اسپورلئان را به دست آورد. 14-3. جوان 22 ساله، 7 فوت 4 اینچ (2. 24 متر) مرد فرانسوی 20 شوت از 29 شوت از زمین، 5 از 11 شوت از محدوده سه امتیازی، و 5 شوت بلاک، 4 توپ ربایی و یک پاس گل در 32 دقیقه در روز شنبه در زمین انجام داد. سن آنتونیو برای چهاردهمین بار در 15 بازی پیروز شد و ومبانیاما با کمترین 3-5 امتیاز از فصل 197 به سومین بازیکن NBA تبدیل شد. چهار توپ ربایی و پنج بلوک در یک بازی. ومبانیاما گفت: «این بسیار خاص است، اما برخلاف بسیاری از همتایانم، من در آمارگیری خیلی خوب نیستم.» ومبانیاما از امتیاز بالای 52 امتیازی خود در دوران حرفه ای خود خجالتی بود که در 4 نوامبر در پیروزی مقابل دالاس به دست آورد. «ومبی» در کوارتر اول 17 امتیاز به دست آورد، در حالی که اسپرز با 29 امتیاز برتری داشت و 29 امتیاز به بیش از 3 رسید. 13 ریباند در نیمه دوم با پیش افتادن سن آنتونیو 61-45. میچ جانسون، سرمربی اسپرز گفت: «فکر می‌کردم او بازی را تهاجمی شروع کرد و فکر می‌کردم که او سعی می‌کند با قدرت زیادی به صورت تهاجمی بازی کند، به‌ویژه، فقط از نظر تصاحب املاک و تلاش برای رسیدن به حاشیه.»

Karl-Anthony Towns keeps drawing praise from his former coaches.

Yet another one pointed out how Towns — by playing a central role in the Knicks’ championship — disproved much of the criticism that surrounded him throughout his career.

“When we first got him in Minnesota, the playoffs, they were saying how he’s a very good player that couldn’t win, couldn’t get the team to the playoffs,” Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori, who served as an assistant with the Timberwolves when Towns was there, said before the Knicks’ 97-96 buzzer-beating win Saturday night at Madison Square Garden. “Then, when we got to the playoffs, any time we struggled, it was him that took the fall, unfairly. And I think it was great to see not only the impact that he had on this championship team, but to see the way that he’s playing now. … I love KAT; I was happy for him to get to the mountaintop; I was happy for him to play a major role.

“Then, when we made a deep run, they said you can’t win a title with him, and he got the blame.”

Earlier this week, Timberwolves coach Chris Finch shared while the Knicks were in Minnesota a similar sentiment about Towns, who missed Saturday’s game due to an illness, shedding a narrative that he isn’t a winner.

“Particularly when he started his playoff journey, how much flak he had gotten,” Finch said.

“It was fun to see him at the heart of it too, especially as they were kind of tweaking their offense going along and all of his skills came to the surface through that.”

Jordan Clarkson, who missed Saturday’s game due to right plantar fasciitis, was wearing a boot on his right foot while sitting on the Knicks bench.

OG Anunoby was out Saturday due to left calf soreness.

Towns’ absence meant a significant role for James Wiseman, who logged 24 minutes off the bench and recorded five points, six rebounds and three blocks.

“I thought James was great,” head coach Mike Brown said. “He ran the floor in both directions, he talked defensively, he impacted the ball at the rim in a phenomenal way. I thought he was really good in his minutes.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has died. He was 89.

His family announced his death Saturday, describing him as “the greatest jeweler of our time” and praising his humanity and entrepreneurial talent.

Bulgari presided for decades over a brand celebrated by supermodels, Hollywood stars and collectors for its bold designs and distinctive use of color.

Born in Rome in 1937, he was the grandson of Sotirios Voulgaris, who founded the jewelry business after leaving Greece.

Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewelry, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome, adapting both his craft and his family name to his new home.

Paolo Bulgari joined the family business shortly after leaving school. Working alongside his father, Giorgio, he initially focused on precious stones, developing an expertise in gemstones that would inform his work as a designer and businessman throughout his career.

Turning away from the delicate aesthetic associated with Parisian jewelry houses, the Bulgari family embraced bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions and unexpected combinations of color.

Drawing inspiration from ancient Rome and Italy’s artistic heritage, the distinctive style helped set the brand apart internationally.

Alongside his brother Nicola and nephew Francesco Trapani, Bulgari led the company’s expansion into major luxury markets, opening stores in New York, Paris, Geneva and Monte Carlo.

The business diversified beyond jewelry into watches, perfumes, leather goods and, eventually, hotels.

Heading the group since the mid-1980s, Bulgari guided the company through a period of significant international growth. Its jewelry was a fixture on celebrities spanning from Elizabeth Taylor to Zendaya.

Tall and silver-haired, he occasionally appeared alongside the stars wearing his creations, maintaining a characteristically reserved presence.

In 2011, the family sold a controlling stake in the company to French luxury conglomerate LVMH in a deal valued at more than $5 billion, ending decades of direct family control.

Despite his association with the glamorous world of international luxury, Bulgari frequently referred to his family’s humble start.

In 2019, he and his wife established the Paolo Bulgari Foundation to support young people through schooling and job training in disadvantaged neighborhoods on the outskirts of Rome.

“Many people don’t know it,” he wrote in the foundation’s introduction, “but at the origin of my surname there is a story of migration.”

His funeral will be held Monday at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Rome.
news.content: پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. پائولو بولگاری، نوه یک نقره‌ساز یونانی که به تبدیل کسب و کار خانوادگی جواهرات به یک برند لوکس جهانی مترادف با زرق و برق و طراحی ایتالیایی کمک کرد، درگذشت. او 89 سال داشت. خانواده‌اش روز شنبه درگذشت او را اعلام کردند و او را "بزرگترین جواهرساز زمان ما" توصیف کردند و انسانیت و استعداد کارآفرینی او را تحسین کردند. بولگاری برای دهه‌ها ریاست برندی را بر عهده داشت که توسط سوپرمدل‌ها، ستاره‌های هالیوود و کلکسیونرها به دلیل طرح‌های جسورانه و استفاده متمایز از رنگ‌ها مورد تحسین قرار می‌گرفت. او در سال 1937 در رم به دنیا آمد و نوه سوتیریوس ولگاریس بود که پس از ترک یونان، تجارت جواهرات را تأسیس کرد. ولگاریس که اصالتاً اهل پارامیتیا، دهکده ای کوهستانی در منطقه اپیروس در شمال غربی یونان است که به جواهرات نقره اش مشهور است، از حکومت عثمانی گریخت و پیش از افتتاح مغازه در رم در ناپل اقامت گزید و هنر و نام خانوادگی خود را با خانه جدیدش تطبیق داد. پائولو بولگاری مدت کوتاهی پس از ترک مدرسه به تجارت خانوادگی پیوست. او که در کنار پدرش جورجیو کار می‌کرد، در ابتدا بر روی سنگ‌های قیمتی تمرکز کرد و در سنگ‌های قیمتی تخصص داشت که به کار او به‌عنوان یک طراح و تاجر در طول زندگی حرفه‌ای‌اش کمک می‌کرد. خانواده بولگاری با رویگردانی از زیبایی‌شناسی ظریف مرتبط با خانه‌های جواهرات پاریس، از سنگ‌های قیمتی جسورانه، ترکیب‌های طلای زرد غنی و رنگ‌های متفاوت استفاده کردند. با الهام گرفتن از روم باستان و میراث هنری ایتالیا، سبک متمایز به شما کمک می کند

news.originalContent:
Behind Somalia’s break with the UAE lies a domestic power struggle with regional leaders close to Abu Dhabi.

Three years ago, at a town hall meeting in Mogadishu, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud defended one of his country’s most controversial foreign partnerships.

The United Arab Emirates, he declared, was “one of the greatest pillars” of Somalia’s war against the al-Qaeda-linked armed group al-Shabab. He praised Abu Dhabi’s support for the country’s armed forces despite longstanding concerns about its political influence.

Having returned to power in 2022, Mohamud sought to repair relations with the Gulf state after a period of strained ties under his predecessor, while reassuring a sceptical Somali public that the UAE’s involvement was a boon rather than a hindrance.

This year, that relationship unravelled spectacularly.

On November 19, Somalia ordered the Emirati ambassador to leave the country and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, marking the sharpest rupture yet in a relationship that had shifted from close security cooperation and deep commercial ties to open hostility.

The UAE said it had already withdrawn its diplomatic staff from Mogadishu in January.

The decision came 10 months after Somalia annulled several commercial, defence and security agreements with the UAE, accusing its former ally of undermining its sovereignty.

In a sharp public rebuke two days before the expulsion order, Mohamud accused the UAE of heightening political divisions, financing rival regional administrations and supporting armed actors operating beyond the federal government’s control.

“A brother does not burn your house. A brother does not buy your property without your knowledge. A brother does not divide your family,” he said.

“After years of diplomatic engagement, the Federal Government assesses that UAE policies threaten Somalia’s national security,” Awes Hagi Yusuf Ahmed, Somalia’s national security adviser (NSA), said in a post on X.

The UAE hit back, accusing Mogadishu of allowing its internal political disputes to strain bilateral ties, in an apparent reference to the president’s contentious relations with some of Somalia’s semi-autonomous regional administrations, which maintain close ties with Abu Dhabi.

Anwar Gargash, a senior Emirati official, said the UAE’s ties with Somalia would “remain deeper and stronger” despite the president’s criticism.

The diplomatic rupture comes amid an escalating domestic power struggle between Mohamud and regional leaders resisting his efforts to reassert federal authority, several of whom have cultivated close ties with Abu Dhabi.

It also marks a striking reversal for a president during whose first term the UAE significantly expanded its foothold in Somalia and who later emerged as one of Abu Dhabi’s strongest defenders.

Somalia’s efforts to rebuild national institutions since the establishment of a permanent federal government in 2012 have unfolded alongside the consolidation of regional administrations that retain considerable autonomy and political power.

Abu Dhabi’s ties with Mogadishu deepened during Mohamud’s first presidency, from 2012 to 2017.

The UAE reopened its embassy in the capital in 2014, and Mohamud inaugurated a UAE-funded military training centre for Somali forces the following year.

At the same time, the Gulf state cultivated commercial, security and diplomatic ties with regional administrations, including Puntland and Jubbaland, as well as Somaliland, which declared independence from Somalia in 1991.

The UAE is also one of Somalia’s most important trading partners, serving as an important source of imports and a hub for Somali businesses trading in international markets.

But its influence extends well beyond trade, with big investments in infrastructure and security concentrated in Somaliland, Puntland and Jubbaland.

Among the most visible of these investments is Berbera port in Somaliland, where Dubai’s state-owned port operator DP World has invested heavily in expanding the facility and developing a trade corridor connecting it to Ethiopia and the wider region.

Through its subsidiary P&O Ports, the company also operates Bosaso port in Puntland, with both ports providing crucial sources of revenue for their respective administrations.

Somaliland’s Foreign Minister Abdirahman Dahir Adam said the UAE treated it as an independent state, making it an attractive partner, while Emirati investments had created jobs and improved regional connectivity.

“The UAE saw Somaliland’s potential early and backed that view with real investment,” Adam told Al Jazeera.

“The impact on our economy has been significant. DP World’s development of Berbera Port and the Berbera Corridor has turned Berbera into a serious regional gateway,” he added.

Their strategic location along the Gulf of Aden also gives Somaliland and Puntland considerable leverage, making them attractive partners for foreign powers seeking a foothold along one of the world’s busiest shipping routes.

The UAE has developed military facilities near both ports, while in Puntland it helped establish and fund the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF), initially an antipiracy unit that has since become an important counterterrorism force.

More recently, it has supported Puntland’s campaign against ISIL (ISIS) in Somalia with drone attacks and carried out a strike this year against al-Shabab in support of Puntland’s forces, a security official in the region told Al Jazeera.

Abu Dhabi maintains similar commercial and security ties with Jubbaland, which borders Kenya, although the extent of its involvement there is less publicly documented.

A senior Puntland official speaking anonymously told Al Jazeera the UAE’s interventions had helped regional states consolidate their authority, with no equivalent assistance coming from the federal government. “It is obvious why on that level the UAE is a more important partner,” the official said.

Aweis Ahmed, a Somalia expert at Chatham House, told Al Jazeera that while Emirati support had brought tangible benefits to Somalia’s regional states, it had also strengthened their position against the federal government, undermining Mogadishu’s efforts to assert its authority.

“They view these things differently. On the one hand, it helps the peripheries, whilst it undermines the centre,” Ahmed said.

That partnership suffered a setback after Mohamud left office in 2017, when his successor, Mohamed Abdullahi, also known as Farmaajo, refused to take sides in a diplomatic dispute between the UAE and Saudi Arabia on one side and Qatar on the other.

Relations improved after Mohamud returned to power in 2022, but tensions persisted over Abu Dhabi’s increasingly independent dealings with regional administrations, often bypassing the federal government entirely.

Abdinor Dahir, director of the Somalia-based Adkaysi Institute for Research, Peace and Inclusive Resilience, told Al Jazeera that the UAE’s relationships with regional states had deepened disagreements over who had the authority to conclude agreements with foreign partners.

“Overall, the regional states’ external relationship with the UAE and the resulting disputes weaken federal authority, undermine counterterrorism cooperation, and risk turning foreign policy into a permanent source of internal conflict,” Dahir said.

The dispute came to a head in January, when Mogadishu annulled its agreements with Abu Dhabi, accusing the UAE of secretly transporting an Emirati-backed Yemeni separatist leader through Somaliland without authorisation.

Somaliland, Puntland and Jubbaland rejected the announcement, insisting their agreements with Abu Dhabi, particularly over ports, would remain in force.

NSA Yusuf Ahmed accused the regional administrations of compromising national security through their independent dealings with Abu Dhabi.

“Port agreements for Berbera, Bosaso and Kismayo, concluded outside federal authority, take strategic infrastructure out of national control,” he said in a post on X. “That is a security question, not a political one.”

But the dispute with the UAE has also become entangled with a wider struggle over political power within Somalia, as Mohamud’s efforts to strengthen the central government through constitutional and electoral changes have met resistance from regional leaders.

Puntland and Jubbaland, both federal member states, have opposed changes they say would weaken their autonomy, while functionally independent Somaliland has long rejected Mogadishu’s authority.

Somali officials have also accused the UAE of backing the deposed leader of Southwest State, Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen, who has fought to retake several towns around the regional capital, Baidoa, in recent months.

Laftagareen told Al Jazeera that he would remove Mohamud’s ally, who took power following a contested election in Baidoa.

Aweis Ahmed, the Chatham House expert, told Al Jazeera the UAE’s support for Mohamud’s domestic opponents had helped them thwart his efforts to push through contentious constitutional and electoral changes.

“This issue with the UAE is more about the local dynamics than some big question about sovereignty for Hassan Sheikh,” he said.

“A direct line to Abu Dhabi gives these sub-national leaders more room to pursue their own priorities when relations with Mogadishu are difficult,” Dahir said.

However, Aweis Ahmed warned that the UAE’s involvement, along with that of other powers from the Middle East, was deepening domestic divisions while drawing Somali actors into wider regional disputes.

“They have made important contributions, but overall their involvement is exacerbating Somalia’s internal and external issues,” he said.

The federal government has aligned itself closely with Turkiye, Qatar and Egypt, while some regional administrations have cultivated ties with the UAE and Ethiopia, and Somaliland has drawn closer to Israel.

“These countries have their own issues, and they’re overlapping with Somalia’s internal rivalries,” Aweis Ahmed said.

At home, Mogadishu has increasingly deployed its growing military strength, including Turkish-trained troops, against UAE-aligned rivals opposed to Mohamud’s constitutional and electoral agenda.

Turkish-trained federal forces helped remove Southwest State leader Abdiaziz Hassan Laftagareen from power, while a similar attempt to dislodge Jubbaland’s Ahmed Mohamed Islam, also known as Madobe, following his disputed re-election in 2024 failed.

In Puntland, tensions with Mogadishu prompted regional forces to seize several federal military bases and expel federal institutions.

Beyond Somalia, Sudan has complained to Mogadishu about the UAE’s alleged use of facilities in the port cities of Bosaso and Berbera to supply the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group fighting the Sudanese army.

A Somali source told Al Jazeera that Sudan’s intelligence chief raised the issue during a visit to Mogadishu in 2025, pressing Somali officials to at least publicly condemn the alleged supply operations if they were unable to stop them.

In early November, Yassir al-Atta, the Sudanese army chief of staff, went further, alleging that fighters from northern Somalia had taken part in the conflict alongside the RSF.

The passage of Abu Dhabi-backed Yemeni separatist leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi through Somali territory has similarly drawn Mogadishu into tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen.
news.content: در پس جدایی سومالی از امارات متحده عربی، جنگ قدرت داخلی با رهبران منطقه نزدیک به ابوظبی نهفته است. سه سال پیش، در جلسه تالار شهر در موگادیشو، حسن شیخ محمد، رئیس جمهور سومالی از یکی از بحث برانگیزترین مشارکت های خارجی کشورش دفاع کرد. او اعلام کرد امارات متحده عربی "یکی از بزرگ ترین جنگ ها" بود. گروه مسلح الشباب وابسته به القاعده. او حمایت ابوظبی از نیروهای مسلح این کشور را علیرغم نگرانی های طولانی مدت در مورد نفوذ سیاسی آن ستود. محمد پس از بازگشت به قدرت در سال 2022، پس از یک دوره تیره شدن روابط در دوره سلف خود، به دنبال ترمیم روابط با کشور خلیج فارس بود، در حالی که به مردم سومالی نسبت به این که این رابطه یک سال بود و نه یک سال تقویت بود، اطمینان داد. به طرز تماشایی باز شد در 19 نوامبر، سومالی به سفیر امارات دستور داد کشور را ترک کند و سفیر خود را از ابوظبی فراخواند که شدیدترین گسست تاکنون در روابطی است که از همکاری نزدیک امنیتی و روابط عمیق تجاری به خصومت آشکار تغییر کرده بود. این تصمیم 10 ماه پس از آن اتخاذ شد که سومالی چندین قرارداد تجاری، دفاعی و امنیتی با امارات متحده عربی را لغو کرد و متحد سابق خود را به تضعیف حاکمیت خود متهم کرد. محمد در یک توبیخ عمومی تند دو روز قبل از دستور اخراج، امارات را به تشدید اختلافات سیاسی متهم کرد.

news.originalContent:
There is enough justified anger among the British youth to spark a wave of mass protests.

The protests engulfing Europe represent a new level of popular mobilisation quite unlike any historical precedent. In France, Spain, Italy, Serbia, Germany and other countries across the continent, mass movements are challenging austerity and government failures.

On Friday, the United Kingdom saw what is likely to be the beginning of its own wave of youth-driven demonstrations. Thousands of students walked out of hundreds of schools and universities around the country, from Aberdeen to Brighton, Swansea to Nottingham, making it one of the largest student mobilisations since the tripling of tuition fees back in 2010.

The protests were called by organisations involved in the International Conference Against War, a pan-European initiative aimed at coordinating the movements against militarism. The University and College Union (UCU) was the first union to back the initiative with a National Day of Action, urging members across the university sector to hold protests and rallies alongside students.

That major unions followed UCU in supporting the walkouts, including Unison, Unite, the National Education Union (NEU), GMB and the Educational Institute of Scotland (EIS), speaks to the potential of union support.

In London, demonstrations from universities and colleges converged on Trafalgar Square to chants of “fight for our future, not their wars” before moving to Downing Street to hear student activists and trade union leaders berate the government for prioritising defence spending over education and public services.

There is indeed much for British youth to be angry about. Like in the rest of Europe, young people in the UK are facing a convergence of high inflation, unemployment, economic stagnation, the gutting of public services and deteriorating living standards, including a housing crisis stoked by property speculation. Combined with police brutality over solidarity with Palestine, unrestrained racism and sexism and expectations of environmental and climate catastrophe, mass protest is rather predictable.

According to government estimates, close to one million people between 16 and 24 years of age are “Neets” – not in education, employment or training; this is more than 13 percent of that age group. Young people make up more than 40 percent of the unemployed in the country. Apart from a tough job market, there is also a rampant mental health epidemic and an education system that few can afford.

Here we have the makings of a social and economic crisis waiting to happen, and yet the government response has been to seek more austerity.

It is a wonder that Alan Milburn, former Labour minister responsible for introducing private finance into the NHS in the late 1990s, was commissioned to write the controversial report on Neets for the government. Why bother to provide welfare when the private sector can solve the crisis? Unsurprisingly, Milburn’s recommendations are market-focused and include cutting certain benefits for youth, including for those with disabilities.

This comes on top of years of austerity in the higher education sector. Job cuts and course closures have become standard responses from university managements dealing with the lack of direct government funding. Many describe it as academic vandalism. What funding cuts have produced is extreme dysfunction, chaos and mismanagement: Faustian bargains with banks, management consultants and corporate outsourcing that serve efficiency and profit over quality provision.

While education and civilian job openings are dwindling, British youth are offered more opportunities in the army, which is now promoting a fully paid 18-month “foundation scheme”.

Military training, bolstered by a public campaign around “warfighting readiness” as part of last year’s Strategic Defence Review, was the brainchild of ministers under Keir Starmer, one of the most unpopular prime ministers in British history. True to form, Starmer pushed through an additional 15 billion pounds ($19.6bn) towards defence immediately before leaving office, for a total of 298 billion pounds ($389.8bn) over four years.

This is a worrying trend across Europe: While there are diminishing funds for public services, military spending is shooting up. This fact has not been lost on young people.

But what is driving this rearmament frenzy is that the European project is increasingly being bound together by NATO, along with Trump’s insistence that the EU should pay its fair share in maintaining the alliance. Support for Ukraine against Russia is at the centre of that project.

If youth mobilisation in the UK reaches the same level as in France, for example, this could be the first major test of Andy Burnham’s government. The French revolt was started over education – not the first strikes in French history over education, considering the origins of the 1968 uprisings. Still, France spends 5.1 percent of GDP on education.

The UK spends 4.1 percent of GDP on education, and even part of this budget has been diverted to defence, with less funding for schools in the coming years.

The UK has had seven prime ministers in the past decade, each one unable to deliver desperately needed income and wealth redistribution. A decade of Tory prime ministers allowed the rich to get very rich. Starmer continued the tradition. He was hammered by Reform and the Greens in the last local elections, firstly because he was unable to come through on the social democratic promises that many were hoping a Labour government would provide.

But second, he failed to recognise the genuine anger over British complicity in the Palestinian genocide, and then responded to mass protest with punitive legislation. Notwithstanding the Burnham bounce, the sitting prime minister has stuck to the same tack as his predecessor. His new foreign secretary has admitted that the government got it wrong over Palestine, but this needs to be backed up by action.

As Burnham faces growing protest, a heavy-handed approach will not work. Nor will more neoliberal reforms. A half-century of privatisation, deregulation and cuts to social welfare has produced the current malaise, and the crisis is only deepening.

The youth and the rest of European society are demanding change – real, lasting change in the political and economic spheres.

The revolutions that convulsed Europe in 1848 were a response to severe economic crisis, unemployment and bad harvests that caused famine. The European protests today unfold under comparable conditions. The task of those who want to see change is an internationalism that can generalise grievances, coordinate the movements and deliver concrete solidarity against austerity and war.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.
news.content: به اندازه کافی خشم موجه در میان جوانان بریتانیایی وجود دارد که موجی از اعتراضات گسترده را برانگیزد. تظاهراتی که اروپا را فراگرفته نشان دهنده سطح جدیدی از بسیج مردمی است که کاملاً شبیه هیچ سابقه تاریخی نیست. در فرانسه، اسپانیا، ایتالیا، صربستان، آلمان و سایر کشورهای سراسر قاره، جنبش‌های توده‌ای ریاضت اقتصادی و شکست‌های دولت را به چالش می‌کشند. روز جمعه، بریتانیا شاهد چیزی بود که احتمالاً آغاز موج تظاهرات جوانان خود را آغاز خواهد کرد. هزاران دانش آموز از صدها مدرسه و دانشگاه در سراسر کشور، از آبردین تا برایتون، سوانسی تا ناتینگهام خارج شدند، که این امر آن را به یکی از بزرگترین بسیج دانشجویی از زمان افزایش سه برابری شهریه ها در سال 2010 تبدیل کرده است. این اعتراضات توسط سازمان‌های درگیر در کنفرانس بین‌المللی علیه جنگ، یک ابتکار پاناروپایی با هدف هماهنگی جنبش‌ها علیه میلیتاریسم برگزار شد. اتحادیه دانشگاه و کالج (UCU) اولین اتحادیه ای بود که از ابتکار عمل با روز ملی اقدام حمایت کرد و از اعضای بخش دانشگاه خواست تا در کنار دانشجویان تظاهرات و تجمعات برگزار کنند. این که اتحادیه‌های بزرگ از UCU در حمایت از انصراف‌ها پیروی کردند، از جمله Unison، Unite، اتحادیه ملی آموزش (NEU)، GMB و موسسه آموزشی اسکاتلند (EIS)، از پتانسیل حمایت از اتحادیه‌ها سخن می‌گوید. در لندن، تظاهرات دانشگاه‌ها و کالج‌ها در میدان ترافالگار گرد هم آمدند تا شعارهای «برای آینده ما بجنگید» قبل از حرکت به سمت جنگ‌هایشان.

news.originalContent:
در پی آتش‌سوزی در یک کارخانه شیرینی‌پزی در غرب جاوه در روز شنبه، دست‌کم سه نفر کشته شده و ۳۶ نفر همچنان مفقود هستند.

آتش‌نشانان تا امروز همچنان در حال مهار شعله‌های آتش این کارخانه بودند و همزمان امدادگران در بخش‌هایی از ساختمان آسیب‌دیده که گمان می‌رود کارگران در آن محبوس شده باشند، به دنبال مفقودان می‌گردند.

آژانس ملی جست‌وجو و نجات اندونزی روز یکشنبه اعلام کرد که ۱۵ نفر از بازماندگان پیدا شده‌اند و چهار نفر دیگر با جراحات نامشخص به بیمارستان و یک درمانگاه محلی منتقل شده‌اند.

این کارخانه در منطقه سرانگ، استان بانتن، در حدود ۵۰ کیلومتری غرب جاکارتا، پایتخت اندونزی واقع شده است.

مقامات محلی و کشوری هنوز علت این آتش‌سوزی را اعلام نکرده‌اند.

آندرا سونی، فرماندار بانتن، به رسانه‌ها گفت که گمان می‌رود حدود ۶۰ نفر هنگام آتش‌سوزی در کارخانه حضور داشته‌ و مشغول کار بوده‌اند.

عکس‌ها و فیلم‌هایی که از این حادثه منتشر شده، شعله‌های آتش را در این کارخانه بزرگ در طول شب نشان می‌دهد و آتش‌نشان‌ها که در حال تلاش برای مقابله با شعله‌هاهستند.

امدادگران صبح یکشنبه حداقل یک جسد را از میان آوار بیرون کشیده‌اند.

آژانس ملی جست‌وجو و نجات اندونزی اعلام کرد: «اعضای تیم مشترک امداد و نجات تمام تلاش خود را برای یافتن قربانیان مفقود شده انجام می‌دهند و در عین حال ایمنی پرسنل حاضر در محل را در اولویت قرار می‌دهند.»

براساس گزارش‌های محلی بستگان کارگران مفقود شده در بیرون کارخانه جمع شده و منتظر دریافت اطلاعات هستند.

شبکه تلویزیونی کومپاس به نقل از توبوگاس ماچفودز، مسئول آتش‌نشانی منطقه، گزارش داد که آتش‌نشانان ساعت ۱۶:۳۰ به وقت محلی به ساختمان فراخوانده شده‌اند، اما ساختمان از قبل در شعله‌های آتش فرو رفته بود.

وی گفت: «وقتی ما به محل رسیدیم ... منطقه وسیعی از قبل در آتش سوخته بود. بنابراین ما نمی‌توانستیم تشخیص دهیم که آیا سیستم حفاظتی شرکت به درستی کار می‌کند یا خیر.»

به گفته مقامات جستجو و نجات، این کارخانه متعلق به شرکت پی‌تی فنوسا اگونگ مولیا است که در لینکدین خود را زیرمجموعه شرکت یونیفام، یکی از بزرگترین شرکت‌های مواد غذایی و آشامیدنی اندونزی، معرفی کرده است.

A pair of spacecraft slipped into orbit around Mercury on Saturday after an eight-year cruise through the inner solar system to unravel our littlest planet’s mountain of mysteries.

The linked robotic explorers — one European, the other Japanese — will separate from one another next month in order to map and study the scorching little planet from different altitudes.

The $2 billion mission is known collectively as BepiColombo.

The European Space Agency announced BepiColombo’s arrival via social media.

A series of thruster firings slowed the spacecraft enough to be captured by the planet’s weak gravity.

But it took several anxious hours before flight controllers in Germany — 94 million miles away — could confirm that BepiColombo had achieved orbit.

Teams pored over the data streaming back; additional information was not immediately available.

BepiColombo is only the third spacecraft to visit Mercury — the sun’s closest planet and barely bigger than our moon — and the first in more than a decade.

NASA’s Mariner 10 flew past Mercury three times in the mid-1970s. The team included the late Italian mathematician Giuseppe “Bepi” Colombo, for whom this latest mission is named.

NASA’s Messenger spacecraft entered orbit around Mercury in 2011 and, after running out of fuel, crashed into the planet in 2015.

Launched in 2018, BepiColombo took a slower, more roundabout route to get to Mercury, flying once past Earth, twice past Venus and six times past Mercury for gravity-guiding assists.

All those loop-de-loops put more than 6 billion miles on the odometer. The conjoined spacecraft shed their mother ship in September for the final leg of the journey.

Lead project scientist Geraint Jones said he and others can’t wait for all the new data to start streaming down in the spring.

The mission will provide the ability to compare “unprecedented measurements taken by two spacecraft at the planet at the same time,” he noted.

Once orbiting separately, the European Space Agency’s satellite and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s smaller craft will study Mercury’s dense interior and exterior magnetic field, as well as everything in between: impact craters, volcanic plains, mountain ridges and peaks jutting as high as 3 miles.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یک جفت فضاپیما پس از هشت سال گشت و گذار در داخل منظومه شمسی برای کشف کوه اسرار کوچکترین سیاره ما، روز شنبه به مدار عطارد افتاد. کاوشگران رباتیک مرتبط - یکی اروپایی و دیگری ژاپنی - ماه آینده به منظور نقشه برداری و مطالعه سیاره کوچک سوزان مختلف از یکدیگر جدا می شوند. این ماموریت 2 میلیارد دلاری در مجموع به عنوان BepiColombo شناخته می شود. آژانس فضایی اروپا از طریق رسانه های اجتماعی ورود BepiColombo را اعلام کرد. مجموعه ای از شلیک های رانشگر سرعت فضاپیما را به اندازه ای کاهش داد که توسط گرانش ضعیف سیاره گرفته شود. اما چندین ساعت اضطراب طول کشید تا کنترل کننده های پرواز در آلمان - 94 میلیون مایل یا سانتیگراد - Beolo بتوانند به این موضوع دست یابند. تیم‌ها به جریان برگشتی داده‌ها پرداختند. اطلاعات اضافی فوراً در دسترس نبود. BepiColombo تنها سومین فضاپیمایی است که از عطارد - نزدیکترین سیاره خورشید و به سختی بزرگتر از ماه ما - بازدید می کند و اولین بار در بیش از یک دهه گذشته است. Mariner 10 ناسا در اواسط دهه 1970 سه بار از کنار عطارد عبور کرد. این تیم شامل ریاضیدان فقید ایتالیایی جوزپه "بیپی" کلمبو بود که این آخرین ماموریت برای او نامگذاری شده است. فضاپیمای مسنجر ناسا در سال 2011 وارد مدار عطارد شد و پس از تمام شدن سوخت، در سال 2015 به این سیاره برخورد کرد. BepiColombo که در سال 2018 به فضا پرتاب شد، مسیر آهسته‌تر و دوربرگردان‌تری را برای رسیدن به عطارد طی کرد، یک بار از کنار زمین، دو بار از سوی V پرواز کرد.

British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes.

But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn’t prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the Strait of Hormuz while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby.

Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the war with Iran threatens the area’s habitat and wildlife.

Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the UN logo, the athlete started from the Musandam peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 9.3 miles in total.

Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started.

The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea.

“I looked up and I could see that an oil tanker about four kilometers away had been hit,” he told the Associated Press after he returned to London. “The explosion was so loud, two booms, and then fighter jets coming in. And at that moment I realized we have to get out of here right now.”

Pugh, 56, managed to finish his feat after more stops and starts, including passing another vessel that sent fireballs into the sky after it was attacked.

“Most people, when they think about the Strait of Hormuz, they think of a shipping lane,” he said. “But it is also one of the most beautiful places I have ever been … it’s one of the treasure troves of the natural world.”

“With all these ships being sunk, this area is under severe threat,” he added. “It’s going to take years, decades for this area to recover.”

Iran has in recent weeks increased attacks on vessels that it claimed traveled along unauthorized routes in the strait as it seeks to impose its control on the crucial waterway, where a fifth of all oil traded passed through before the US and Israel launched the war on Feb. 28.

Several tankers have also struck sea mines laid by Tehran, in some cases exploding and bursting into flames, among them one that was carrying over 2 million barrels of oil last month.

Pugh warned of how oil leaking from the dozens of tankers damaged since February could create lasting problems for the region’s animals, as well as its coastlines, coral reefs and mangrove forests.

He described seeing large numbers of dolphins following his boat as he sailed in, as well as turtles and ospreys. He also marveled at the hundreds of turtles he saw during a swim along the Omani coast before the war.

“When oil gets in there, when chemical pollution gets in there, it becomes very, very difficult to clean up that type of mess,” he said. “It lasts for generations.”

Pugh has had plenty of experience facing extreme temperatures and predators, including great white sharks. But swimming in a conflict zone presented entirely new dangers.

To stay safe, the challenge was done in sections over three days, with a total of about six and a half hours of swimming. The athlete recalled seeing a gas carrier being struck as he returned to the harbor on the second day.

“I’ll never ever forget going past that gas carrier, the smell of the chemicals and then the flames, they were literally like fireballs going up into the sky. Around the ship, the water was on fire,” Pugh said.

“And to think of the impact which a casualty like this has on nature — it was very, very acute.”

Pugh has spent much of the past 40 years swimming in places from Antarctica to the Red Sea and the English Channel to urge more action to protect marine environments from climate change, pollution and loss of biodiversity.

He was the first athlete to swim across the North Pole and complete a long-distance swim in every one of the world’s oceans. In 2023, he swam all 315 miles of the Hudson River to highlight the importance of clean rivers.

His foundation says the challenges have helped secure official agreements to protect about 1.35 million square miles of vulnerable ocean.

Some have dubbed Pugh’s blend of epic swimming and political outreach as “Speedo diplomacy.”

“Sport opens doors, it creates dialogue, it enables people to start thinking about these important issues,” Pugh said.

“My message is very simple,” he added. “We’ve got to stop the war. We’ve got to open the strait, and we’ve got to clean up the pollution.”
news.content:
بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. لوئیس پوگ شناگر استقامتی بریتانیایی در قطب شمال و قطب جنوب شنا کرده است تا توجه را به دلایل محیطی جلب کند. اما مبارزه با آب های یخ زده و شرایط شدید او را برای آخرین چالش خود آماده نکرده است: شنا در تنگه هرمز در حالی که نفتکش ها در نزدیکی مورد حمله قرار گرفته و منفجر می شوند. پوگ که حامی اقیانوس‌ها سازمان ملل است، این هفته سه روز را صرف شنا در بخش‌هایی از آبراه خطرناک کرد تا نشان دهد که جنگ با ایران چگونه زیستگاه و حیات وحش منطقه را تهدید می‌کند. این ورزشکار با پوشیدن تنه شنا، عینک و کلاهی با آرم سازمان ملل، از جنوب استراییت، در انتهای شبه جزیره کپه و انتهای شبه‌جزیره شروع کرد. هرمز، در مجموع حدود 9.3 مایل را تکمیل کرد. اعتقاد بر این است که پوگ اولین کسی است که از زمان شروع جنگ در آنجا شنای طولانی مدت انجام داده است. این شناگر گفت که دقایقی پس از ورودش به آب در روز دوشنبه، صدای دو انفجار شدیدی را شنید که دریا را تکان داد. "انفجار بسیار شدید بود، دو بوم و سپس جت های جنگنده وارد شدند. و در آن لحظه متوجه شدم که باید همین الان از اینجا برویم.»
Pugh، 56 ساله، موفق شد شاهکار خود را پس از توقف ها و شروع های بیشتر، از جمله عبور از کشتی دیگری که پس از حمله به آن گلوله های آتشین به آسمان فرستاد، به پایان برساند.

US Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz warned Friday that Russia is suffering “unsustainable” battlefield losses, with monthly deaths outpacing recruitment numbers.

Speaking on “The Brian Kilmeade Show” podcast, Waltz echoed President Trump’s assessment that Russian President Vladimir Putin is “worn down,” arguing the war in Ukraine cannot be won militarily and must end at the negotiating table.

“Right now, the numbers that we have, the Russians are recruiting 20,000 to 25,000 a month of new fresh recruits,” Waltz said. “They’re losing 30,000 to 35,000 a month, dead every single month.

“That is exponentially more than they lost in Afghanistan and approaching what they lost in World War II, a thousand a day,” he added. “It’s just unsustainable.”

The interview followed Trump’s return from Shenzhen, China, where he met with Putin before joining the Russian leader and Chinese President Xi Jinping for the first-ever three-way summit between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China.

The summit produced a joint declaration pledging dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, maintaining stable energy supplies and reforming the United Nations, but the leaders stopped short of announcing breakthroughs on Ukraine or Iran.

At a White House news conference Friday, Trump addressed questions about Putin’s intent regarding the war.

“He’d love to end the war. It’s a very hard thing to do,” Trump said Friday. “To be honest, you have two guys that don’t know how to end it. We’re trying to help them.

“You have two people that hate each other, Zelenskyy and Putin. They don’t know how to end it. They want to end it. They’re both stuck in it,” he added. “And it’s a horrible war, actually. And I thought it would have been maybe one of the easier ones to get ended. But the personalities play.”

Waltz argued that both Ukraine and Russia have “worn each other down,” saying it’s unlikely the two countries will be able to sustain the current level of fighting.

“It’s a horrific war, and the president remains determined to find some construct of a deal that will end it because neither side can sustain this war of attrition,” Waltz said. “There is no winning it militarily. It’s got to end diplomatically.”

Fox News Digital’s Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.
news.content:
مایک والتز، سفیر ایالات متحده در سازمان ملل متحد، روز جمعه هشدار داد که روسیه متحمل خسارات «ناپایدار» در میدان نبرد شده است و تعداد تلفات ماهانه از تعداد سربازگیری فراتر رفته است. والتز که در پادکست «نمایش برایان کیلمید» صحبت می کرد، ارزیابی پرزیدنت ترامپ مبنی بر اینکه ولادیمیر پوتین، رئیس جمهور روسیه «فرسوده شده است» را تکرار کرد و گفت که جنگ در اوکراین را نمی توان از طریق نظامی به دست آورد و باید در میز مذاکره پایان یابد. آنها در حال از دست دادن 30000 تا 35000 در ماه هستند که هر ماه می میرند. او افزود: «این به طور تصاعدی بیشتر از چیزی است که آنها در افغانستان از دست دادند و به چیزی که در جنگ جهانی دوم از دست دادند، روزانه هزار نفر است». "این فقط ناپایدار است."
این مصاحبه پس از بازگشت ترامپ از شنژن چین انجام شد، جایی که وی قبل از پیوستن به رهبر روسیه و رئیس جمهور چین شی جین پینگ برای اولین نشست سه جانبه بین رهبران ایالات متحده، روسیه و چین با پوتین دیدار کرد. این اجلاس بیانیه مشترکی را ارائه کرد که در آن متعهد به گفت‌وگو درباره کاهش خطرات هسته‌ای، حفظ منابع انرژی باثبات و اصلاح سازمان ملل شد، اما رهبران از اعلام پیشرفت‌ها در مورد اوکراین یا ایران کوتاهی کردند. ترامپ روز جمعه در کنفرانس خبری کاخ سفید به سؤالاتی درباره قصد پوتین در مورد جنگ پاسخ داد. صادقانه بگویم، یو

news.originalContent:
Trinity Rodman left in tears after scoring Spirit’s only goal as DiBernardo and Debinha give Current closely-fought win.

Kansas City Current have defeated the Washington Spirit in a closely-contested final to be crowned the NWSL champions for the first time as Trinity Rodman’s bid to avoid a third consecutive final defeat ended in bitter disappointment in Washington, DC.

Vanessa DiBernardo curled in a goal direct from a corner and Brazilian international Debinha added a second in stoppage time to set up Kansas City’s 2-1 victory at Audi Field on Saturday.

Rodman headed in a 98th-minute goal to pull one back for Spirit, but Kansas City held on to win.

“We knew it was going to be a battle; we felt good coming out of the first half,” said DiBernardo, who was named the championship MVP months after returning to professional football following the birth of her daughter.

“We just had to be patient and finish off the game.”

It was another crushing loss for United States star Rodman and her Spirit teammates, who were also beaten in the final in 2025 and 2024.

Rodman, who was in tears at the final whistle, was knocked out of her stride earlier in the game.

The 24-year-old was on the receiving end of a rugged aerial challenge from Kansas City’s Laney Rouse after just five minutes and needed treatment on the sidelines.

Rodman returned to the field grimacing in pain and clutching her shoulder but completed the game.

The opening goal came early in the second half, with DiBernardo’s in-swinging corner looping into the net after Kansas City’s Kayla Sharples cleverly blocked Washington goalkeeper Sandy MacIver.

Deep in stoppage time, Debinha added Current’s second after a sweeping counterattack, before Rodman’s header was too little, too late.

The victory was Kansas City’s first NWSL title after losing in the championship game to the Portland Thorns in 2022.
news.content:
ترینیتی رادمن پس از به ثمر رساندن تنها گل اسپیریت در حالی که دی برناردو و دبینا به کرنت پیروز شدند، گریه کرد. کانزاس سیتی کرنت در یک فینال رقابتی نزدیک، واشنگتن اسپیریت را شکست داد تا برای اولین بار قهرمان NWSL شود، زیرا تلاش ترینیتی رادمن برای جلوگیری از شکست نهایی در یک بازی متوالی واشینگتن. ونسا دی برناردو مستقیماً از روی کرنر به گل رسید و دبینها بازیکن برزیلی یک ثانیه در وقت های تلف شده اضافه کرد تا پیروزی 2-1 کانزاس سیتی را در روز شنبه در آئودی فیلد رقم بزند. رودمن در دقیقه 98 گل دقیقه 98 را با ضربه سر زد تا یک گل برای اسپیریت به عقب برگرداند، اما کانزاس سیتی همچنان پیروز شد. دی برناردو که ماه‌ها پس از بازگشت به فوتبال حرفه‌ای پس از تولد دخترش به عنوان MVP قهرمانی انتخاب شد، گفت: ما می‌دانستیم که این یک نبرد خواهد بود؛ ما از نیمه اول احساس خوبی داشتیم. ما فقط باید صبور باشیم و بازی را تمام کنیم.
این یکی دیگر از باخت های مهیب برای رادمن ستاره ایالات متحده و هم تیمی هایش در اسپریت بود که در سال های 2025 و 2024 نیز در فینال شکست خوردند. رادمن که در سوت پایان اشک می‌ریخت، در اوایل بازی از صحنه خارج شد. این بازیکن 24 ساله تنها پس از 5 دقیقه در یک چالش هوایی ناهموار از لنی روس از کانزاس سیتی قرار داشت و در کناره‌ها نیاز به درمان داشت. رادمن با گریه‌های بداخلاقی به زمین بازگشت، اما نیمه اول بازی را با چنگال به پایان رساند. دی برنارد

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The disgraced Italian cruise ship skipper who abandoned the doomed Costa Concordia, leaving 32 dead off the coast of Italy, has been freed from prison after nine years.

Francesco Schettino, dubbed “Captain Coward,” was released from the Rebibbia Prison in Rome Friday night after a court ruled he successfully passed a rehabilitation and behavior program, Italian newspaper Quotidiano Nazionale reported.

Schettino, 66, will serve out the remaining 7 years of his 16-year sentence on supervised probation after the Rome Surveillance Court’s decision, according to the outlet.

“In our view, all the conditions were in place for this alternative measure to be granted, as it represents the correct continuation of the process after the conviction,” Schettino’s lawyer, Francesca Carnicelli, said.

Schettino was found solely responsible and convicted of manslaughter in the deaths of 32 passengers and crew when the Costa Concordia capsized after ramming into rocks near the Tuscan island of Giglio in the Tyrrhenian Sea on Jan. 13, 2012.

He was convicted in 2015, and his sentence was upheld in 2017, meaning he had served roughly 9 years of the 193-month prison term before his release.

The ill-fated ship, operated by Costa Crociere, had 4,200 passengers and crew on board when it ran aground, striking a reef that left a gash in the hull.

Schettino claimed he had fallen onto a lifeboat during the mad assault of passengers trying to flee the sinking ship.

“The passengers were pouring onto the decks, taking the lifeboats by assault. I didn’t even have a life jacket because I had given it to one of the passengers,” Schettino told Italian daily La Repubblica after the sinking.

“I was trying to get people to get into the boats in an orderly fashion. Suddenly, since the ship was at a 60- to 70-degree angle, I tripped and I ended up in one of the boats. That’s how I found myself there,” he said.

Prosecutors argued Schettino was “cowardly” in his actions, fleeing on a lifeboat to a safe spot and refusing to return to the partially submerged ship after the wreck.

During his trial, Schettino claimed he was the scapegoat used by the Italian cruise line.

“My head was sacrificed to serve economic interests,” the Neapolitan seaman told the court.

Defense attorneys unsuccessfully tried to paint Schettino as a hero, saying his delayed order to abandon ship saved lives.

“If he had given the order to abandon ship right away, a kilometer from the coast, the ship would have been uncontrollable,” attorney Domenico Pepe told an Italian court.

“Not all the lifeboats would have reached the water intact,” he added. “More than 4,000 people could have died.”

Autopsies ruled that a majority of the 32 victims had drowned aboard the ship or after falling into the sea during the chaotic, delayed evacuation.

news.originalContent:
A toxic culture of winning at any cost has been hiding behind the myth of ‘mateship’.

“I knew it was wrong. I knew that using sandpaper was not simply pushing the boundaries of the laws of cricket. It was cheating,” former Australian Test cricketer Cameron Bancroft wrote in a 4,000-word expose.

His frank admission that he knowingly cheated and then lied to investigators and the Australian public was raw.

The footage of Bancroft shoving sandpaper down the front of his trousers, in an attempt to hide his illegal ball tampering during the 2018 Test series between South Africa and Australia, has been seen all over the world; the act of cheating has never been in question.

But the fallout, eight years in the making, no longer centres on a square of sandpaper. It revolves around a culture that placed winning above sound ethics. It created such deep-seated fear that lying – both directly and by omission – became a means to survive, and ultimately exposed the national belief that Australian men’s cricket was underpinned by a sacred sense of “mateship” – standing above self-interest – as a myth.

The basic facts of Australia’s ball-tampering scandal have long been established. Bancroft, with the tacit encouragement of teammate David Warner and under then-captain Steve Smith, who elected to look the other way, executed a premeditated plan to alter the ball’s surface during the third Test in Cape Town, in order to promote reverse swing.

Once he was caught, the public outrage and revulsion were overwhelming. Cricket Australia, the national cricket governing body, rushed through an inadequate investigation, omitting many of the touring party, and concluding that knowledge of the plan was confined to Bancroft, Warner and Smith. It imposed draconian penalties: yearlong bans for Smith and Warner, nine months for Bancroft.

Coach Darren Lehmann eventually stood down, followed out the door by several support staff, administrators and board members.

The cone of silence surrounding the affair cracked open with the release of Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, Sabr, in which he alleged everyone in the dressing room was in on the plan. Players and coaching staff came out publicly to either back Khawaja’s story or reject his version of events.

Current team captain Pat Cummins, who was also part of the team in 2018, publicly insisted that he did not know about the use of sandpaper. This was reportedly the final straw for Bancroft: “It made me feel angry, betrayed and alone,” he wrote.

For eight years he had borne the brunt of being labelled a cheat and watched his former teammates carry on with their Test careers – including Smith and Warner, after serving their bans.

Within hours of Cricket Australia’s announcement of an independent “truth forum” that would provide a “safe place” for discussion – a belated effort to stem the tide of damaging public confessions – Bancroft’s self-penned expose was published in The West Australian newspaper.

Not only did he insist that everyone was in on the scheme, but it was not an isolated occurrence, as the investigation had concluded; he had also used sandpaper in the second Test in Gqeberha that year.

“I made a terrible decision because I wanted to belong in the Australian team,” Bancroft wrote.

The context of his choice shouldn’t be overlooked. He was a 24-year-old adult, yet a junior member of the side playing in his seventh Test, and he desperately wanted to fit in.

The years leading up to the South Africa tour were defined by an increasingly toxic culture in which the boundaries of sportsmanship were tested, stretched and treated as pliable when convenient.

The Australian men’s team were the self-appointed guardians of “the line”, their own behaviour consistently justified as being on the right side of what was acceptable under the mantra of playing “hard but fair”. There was a lack of strong and ethical leadership in the dressing room, from the coaching staff all the way up to the Cricket Australia boardroom.

An independent, wide-ranging review by ethics nonprofit organisation The Ethics Centre, conducted in the aftermath of the affair, exposed a culture of “winning without counting the costs” that seeped throughout Cricket Australia. It was a culture in which staff and players feared the consequences of speaking honestly. It is no wonder that silence and dishonesty flourished in order to protect the brand and ensure self-preservation.

“We were frightened,” Bancroft wrote. “We were under pressure. We were trying to manage a situation that was rapidly getting away from us.”

While the on-field reputation of the Australian Test team has improved since 2018, fronted by captains Tim Paine and then Cummins, the blackened seeds sown were nourished by years of resentment and grievance, and have now emerged fully grown in blighted and twisted ugliness.

The complexity and nuance of ball-tampering have been overtaken by accusations of who knew what and a tug-of-war over who owns the truth – not to mention an administration that desperately hoped a web of half-truths and omissions would hold.

It has held a confronting mirror to the wider public’s veneration of “mateship”, the close bond of brotherhood that Australians have long held as core to their national identity. The baggy green cap worn by the country’s Test cricketers has been its unofficial symbol. Friendship may be universal, but mateship – that’s unique to Australia. The cap looks increasingly frayed with every public disclosure.

For Australians to accept that a young player would consider cheating, and then lie about cheating, as the best way of fitting in with his “mates”, it would mean questioning this idea of national exceptionalism. It would mean accepting that self-interest would trump the sacrosanct bonds of selfless “mateship”.

There have been widespread calls for Australian cricket to move on and a growing collective weariness that this unseemly and unflattering saga continues to dominate the news landscape. Perhaps the reflection in the mirror is simply too confronting to sustain the gaze.

There is an alternate universe in which Cricket Australia, in the aftermath of Newlands, could have stood the three central players down for the final Test, pending a full and thorough investigation that would have included all members of the touring party, rather than a select few. The players could have been supported and could have had the moral fortitude to be completely honest. An open and mature public conversation could have taken place about the nature of ball-tampering and any disciplinary action better reflected the nature of the “crime”. Responsibility could have been shared and Cricket Australia could have accepted its full portion.

It wouldn’t have been easy; it would still have been controversial, but it would likely not have been what is now: an omnishambles of human and reputational wreckage that may yet prematurely end careers.

In 2018, Bancroft thought the Australian team “were down the rabbit hole so far”.

Eight years later, Australian cricket has yet to reckon with its own shortcomings, still stuck in a hole of its own making.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.
news.content: فرهنگ سمی برنده شدن به هر قیمتی در پشت افسانه "همبستگی" پنهان شده است. کامرون بنکرافت، بازیکن سابق کریکت استرالیایی تست در یک پیام 4000 کلمه ای نوشت: "من می دانستم که این اشتباه است. می دانستم که استفاده از کاغذ سنباده صرفاً مرزهای قوانین کریکت را جابجا نمی کند. بلکه تقلب است." مردم استرالیا خام بودند. فیلم بنکرافت در حال هل دادن کاغذ سنباده به جلوی شلوارش، در تلاش برای پنهان کردن دستکاری توپ غیرقانونی خود در طول سری آزمایشی 2018 بین آفریقای جنوبی و استرالیا، در سراسر جهان دیده شده است. عمل تقلب هرگز مورد سوال قرار نگرفته است. این حول فرهنگی می چرخد ​​که برنده شدن را بالاتر از اخلاق صحیح قرار می دهد. این ترس عمیقی ایجاد کرد که دروغگویی - هم مستقیم و هم با حذف - به وسیله ای برای زنده ماندن تبدیل شد و در نهایت این باور ملی را آشکار کرد که کریکت مردان استرالیایی با حس مقدس "همبستگی" - که فراتر از منافع شخصی است - به عنوان یک افسانه استوار است. حقایق اساسی رسوایی دستکاری توپ در استرالیا مدتهاست ثابت شده است. بنکرافت، با تشویق ضمنی هم تیمی دیوید وارنر و زیر نظر کاپیتان آن زمان، استیو اسمیت، که تصمیم گرفت به سمت دیگری نگاه کند، طرحی از پیش طراحی شده برای تغییر سطح توپ در طول آزمایش سوم در کیپ تاون به منظور ترویج چرخش معکوس اجرا کرد. هنگامی که او گرفتار شد، خشم عمومی و دوباره به وجود آمد.
